newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia to sell oil pipeline stake to MOL.
newsitem.headline: Croatia to sell oil pipeline stake to MOL.

text.p: Croatia is close to reaching a deal with the Hungarian oil company MOL for the sale of 12.5 percent in the Adritic crude pipeline operator Janaf for 92.8 million German marks, officials said on Monday.
"The agreement was okayed by the Privatisation Fund board today, but has yet to be approved by the government," a fund vice-president Marija Turudic told Reuters.
The details of the agreement, which has been negotiated for more than a year, were finalised in talks with the Hungarian partner last week, she said.
The purchase price according to the book value will be paid by MOL within 20 days from signing the agreement.
"They also committed themselves to boost their shipments through the Adriatic pipeline," Turudic said.
MOL will have a member on the Janaf board, and there will be a non-discrimination clause in the contract, she said.

Croatian state oil company INA controls 33 percent of Janaf and is currently the main user of the pipeline that runs from the Adriatic port of Omisalj on the island of Krk through central Croatia to Hungary and Eastern Europe.
It operates at some 10-15 percent of its annual 3.5 million tonnes capacity, which industry analysts say could be doubled with minor investments.
Except for 1.5 percent owned by small shareholders, Janaf is controlled by the state. Its book value is put at 743 million marks.

Croatia said earlier this month it was planning to float internationally 30-40 percent of Janaf shares. The government had mandated Deutsche Morgan Grenfell to lead the issue, planned for some six months.
